answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The kernel multiplier is published, charged in delta, and opal lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 3635 identities would post 776 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
